- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias after 10+ consecutive days of high prices; apply downward correction of 1–3% per 3-day window if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- When true outcome shows early downward trend (e.g., 3 consecutive days falling), model often lags; forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per day for next 3 days.
- If sentiment history includes 3+ consecutive negative entries, model tends to overforecast; apply a 3–5% downward bias to forecast mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–3% if sentiment is negative or neutral.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike, model fails to anticipate; add 1–2% downward adjustment for next 3–5 days if sentiment is negative or neutral.
